## 1a357b7e47f96824 · contradiction · high · not-a-defect

**Fact:** Measured 2026-09-28 during the v7.0.673 AGT-160 build, on a tree whose only changes are two NEW files neither test imports: the market agent's --render prints model claude-opus-5 while public.rpc judgment_model() answers {model_id: claude-fable-5-1, reason: lane, fable_pct: 0, fable_share: 42.86} and runner_model_lanes.judgment reads claude-fable-5-1 (updated 2026-09-09). tests/regression/agt-121-market-agent.test.mjs was GREEN in this cycle's baseline and is now RED on that single assertion. Two code paths compute the in-force judgment model and they disagree; fable_pct 0 suggests the renderer applies a budget-driven downgrade that judgment_model() does not report. Outside AGT-160's ownership (no file AGT-160 names is involved), so captured here rather than patched.

**Locations:**
- `tests/regression/agt-121-market-agent.test.mjs:266` — "--render printed model claude-opus-5, the judgment lane runs claude-fable-5-1 (green in the v7.0.673 baseline, red after)"
- `public.runner_model_lanes / rpc judgment_model()` — "lane judgment = claude-fable-5-1; rpc in force = claude-fable-5-1, fable_pct 0, fable_share 42.86"

**Proposed resolution:** Diagnose which path is authoritative and make the market agent's render read the same in-force model judgment_model() returns, so one shared source answers the question for both (pattern:14). If the budget downgrade is deliberate, judgment_model() must report it and agt-121 must assert that reason, not the lane row.

**Ruling:** Refuted on the shipped resolver, read fresh this session. resolveJudgmentModel() in scripts/agent-prompt.js answers from the capability's own model_assignments row FIRST and returns reason 'capability' without ever calling rpc/judgment_model when that model is not the lane's. So --render printing claude-opus-5 while the lane and the RPC read claude-fable-5-1 is the designed answer, not two paths disagreeing, and the fable_pct 0 budget-downgrade guess is wrong because the RPC is not consulted on that path. The real defect is the test's equality expectation, which finding 1969c0e8 carries and which is listed. (devmanager, 2026-09-28)

## 0745194de2f39a50 · other · high · ticketed

**Fact:** TeachScreen falls back to agents[0] for an unknown :agentId while the save posts agent_id from the URL, so /bench/<unknown>/teach renders the first roster agent's identity and stats and files the document under an id no agent holds, destroying the provenance the Teach loop exists to establish.

**Locations:**
- `src/screens/TeachScreen.jsx:81` — "const agent = agents.find(a => a.id === agentId) || agents[0];"
- `src/screens/TeachScreen.jsx:165` — "tenant_id: TENANT_ID, agent_id: agentId,"

**Proposed resolution:** As a trainer, a mistyped or retired agent URL tells me there is no such agent instead of showing me someone else's name and silently filing my document under a dead id. Remove the `|| agents[0]` fallback in src/screens/TeachScreen.jsx: when agents.find() is empty, render a no-such-agent state (or redirect to /bench) and never enable Save; a regression test pins that /bench/nobody/teach issues no /api/load-entries POST. This changes an approved screen's behaviour, so it needs John's call on the treatment (empty state vs redirect) before a kickoff. Surfaced by the Development Manager and the Designer on AGT-164 (2026-09-28); out of AGT-164's scope because Brittany's own roster entry keeps her URL off this path, and pre-existing, not self-made.

**Ruling:** src/screens/TeachScreen.jsx:81 resolves the agent as `agents.find(a => a.id === agentId) || agents[0]`, while the save at :165 posts `agent_id: agentId` straight from the URL. So /bench/<unknown>/teach renders the first roster agent's identity and stats to the trainer and then files what they wrote under an id no agent holds — it destroys exactly the provenance the Teach loop exists to establish, and it does it silently. Pre-existing, not made by the build that surfaced it: the Development Manager and the Designer both hit it on AGT-164 on 2026-09-28, and it sits outside AGT-164's scope because Brittany's own roster entry keeps her URL off this path. / Remove the `|| agents[0]` fallback: when agents.find() comes back empty, tell the trainer there is no such agent — a no-such-agent state or a redirect to /bench — and never enable Save. Pin it with a regression arm asserting /bench/nobody/teach issues no /api/load-entries POST. This changes the behaviour of an approved screen, so the treatment (empty state vs redirect) is your call on a mock before any kickoff; the ticket is filed so the defect is not lost while that call is made. (devmanager, 2026-09-28)

**Locations:**
- `agents:designer` — "designer, "kickoff lacked a fact", on backlog_items:AGT-157, cycle a2d6996b-51a9-4449-9ff6-b3caa6b87752: build needed a fact the kickoff did not carry"

**Proposed resolution:** Skill edit via --promote at the bar

**Ruling:** Nothing grades a kickoff for the facts the build will need: --check-kickoff asserts only the Lanes line, so a missing fact is found by the Builder mid-cycle instead of before the build. At 06:18Z the next cycle's tail read due=true for the same class (0 ratified, 78 proposed), 25 minutes after the loop had run. This cycle declined to run it a second time on the strength of first-hand knowledge rather than the flag."

**Proposed resolution:** Key the gate on when the CLASS LOOP line was written rather than on the writing cycle's started_at — for example by stamping a class_loop_at timestamp, or by widening the notes scan to cycles that ENDED in today's America/Chicago day as well as those that started in it.

**Ruling:** public.class_understanding_due() decides 'already ran today' from the started_at of the cycle whose notes hold the CLASS LOOP line. I read the function body live this session: `where rc.notes ilike '%CLASS LOOP%' and (rc.started_at at time zone 'America/Chicago')::date = (now() at time zone 'America/Chicago')::date`. So a cycle that starts before the America/Chicago day boundary and writes its CLASS LOOP line after it satisfies runner-cycle.md step 7c's rule without satisfying the gate. Measured this week: cycle 6f101f97 started 04:12:08Z, wrote 'CLASS LOOP: P3 - Investor Value, 3 learning claims, synthesis kept' at about 05:5xZ and filed VC-LRN-033/034/035; at 06:18Z the gate read due=true for the same class, 25 minutes later. Only the next cycle's first-hand knowledge stopped a second run - the gate is the only thing the runbook names, so on another night the loop runs twice and files a second set of claims against the same class. / Key the gate on the event instead of a proxy for it (pattern:1): stamp a class_loop_at timestamp when the CLASS LOOP line is written and read the gate off that, or, if the notes scan stays, widen it to cycles that ENDED in today's America/Chicago day as well as those that started in it. Pin it with a regression arm whose writing cycle starts before the boundary and whose CLASS LOOP line is written after it, asserting due=false for that class afterwards. Home: public.class_understanding_due(); runner-cycle.md step 7c states the rule and must name whatever timestamp the gate ends up reading, so the runbook and the gate cannot disagree again. Keep sameChicagoDay()'s reasoning (scripts/ticket-owner.js) as the model for the day arithmetic - a fixed offset is wrong twice a year and silently. (devmanager, 2026-09-28)

Both answers passed the platform's own --dry-run immediately before --apply, so the dry run cannot predict the refusal: it validates against the same stale snapshot. The cost is the whole review turn, roughly 200k tokens of judgment, discarded on an all-or-nothing write -- and re-running invites the same race, because the peer is still filing.

**Locations:**
- `undefined` — "undefined"
- `undefined` — "undefined"

**Proposed resolution:** Scope the coverage requirement to the snapshot the manager was actually shown -- the ids in the --context file -- rather than to the live set at --apply time, and let findings filed after --prepare fall to the next review. That is the same 'rule the queue the manager was shown' principle record_leverage() already enforces for leverage marks. Failing that, have --apply re-read and diff, and refuse only when a SHOWN finding is uncovered, reporting newly-arrived ids as deferred rather than as a refusal.

**Ruling:** apply_audit_review() requires every finding in the LIVE open set to be covered exactly once, while the answer it grades was produced from the snapshot --prepare wrote 10-15 minutes earlier. Under parallel cycles — register B42 makes that the design, not an anomaly — any peer or sub-agent filing a finding in that window invalidates the entire review, all-or-nothing. Failing that, have --apply re-read and diff, refusing only when a SHOWN finding is uncovered and reporting newly-arrived ids as deferred. **Fact:** ARCHITECTURE.md §19v — no before-image, no write. A probe believed to be non-mutating writes without one, so the platform's own safety story for testing destructive paths is false wherever that header is the only guard. Distinct from a PL/pgSQL DO block that ends in RAISE EXCEPTION, which genuinely aborts: this cycle verified its three such probes left the rollback-row count at 41, the cycle count at 729, and an audit_findings ruled_at attributable to devmanager six hours earlier, so that mechanism is sound and only the header is not.

**Locations:**
- `PostgREST Prefer: tx=rollback (no db-tx-end=rollback-allowed) versus every ledger row a probe using it has touched` — "Prefer: tx=rollback is NOT honoured on this PostgREST instance — db-tx-end is not enabled, so the header is silently ignored and the request COMMITS. Measured the hard way this cycle: a PATCH of runner_cycles under that header PERSISTED, leaving api_cost_dev_usd 0.03 and api_cost_qa_usd NULL on live row a4217066-8418-4c1b-9339-40e36797ba10. It hid for eleven versions because every earlier probe of those columns was rejected by the very NOT NULL constraint being probed: the 23502 error aborted the transaction, so nothing persisted and the ignored header LOOKED honoured. The moment AGT-204 made the column nullable, the same probe wrote for real. The phrase "proven without writing anything" was load-bearing in three places: scripts/settle-ship.js and tests/regression/agt-176b-cost-basis.test.mjs (both rewritten at v7.0.637) and AGT-204's own ticket text plus finding e5922187 as reproduced in docs/backlog/BACKLOG-SNAPSHOT.md, which are untouched and still assert it."

**Proposed resolution:** Either enable db-tx-end=rollback-allowed on the PostgREST instance and re-assert that the header aborts, or ban the header from every probe and require the PL/pgSQL DO + RAISE EXCEPTION form, which is proven to abort. Then sweep for the phrase "proven without writing anything" and for tx=rollback across scripts/, tests/ and the ticket store, and correct every claim that rests on it — including AGT-204's own description and finding e5922187.

## ebcd816ec8d62745 · competing-purpose · medium · listed

**Fact:** AGT-194 exists to tell a missing grade apart from a red one — its own ship card says so. A clause vocabulary that cannot express that distinction undercuts the ticket's own purpose, which is why the reason string has to carry it in prose instead.

**Locations:**
- `scripts/verifier.js ciConclusionFinding clause enum (shipped v7.0.631, AGT-194)` — "v7.0.631's ciConclusionFinding fixes its clause enum at four values, so a blocking job that concluded FAILURE is reported under clause cancelled-blocking — the only fit. Seen live on this cycle's own verdict: "[cancelled-blocking] sha e760c795... Tripwire + regression (blocking) = failure". The reason string does say to read each job's actual conclusion rather than the clause, and it distinguishes the two cases in words, but a reader or a later script keying on the clause name will mislabel a real red as a lost grade. Those are opposite facts: a failure is a grade the platform has, a cancellation is a grade it never got."

**Proposed resolution:** Add a fifth clause, failed-blocking, and key it on every blocking job having concluded with at least one failure and no cancellation. The Builder identified this and correctly declined to invent a fifth value the kickoff had fixed at four.
